parallel.requirements: Build an original yq-compatible executable by observing the provided binary and README only, without source lookup, wrapping, or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent launched the yq-explore workflow to delegate behavioral probing and test/spec generation by feature area, then kept final implementation responsibility itself.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote main.go, go.mod, compile.sh, node.go, yamlparse.go, and resolve.go after the workflow, leaving a small partial Go implementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Submission packaging succeeded with a limited source tree, tests, notes, README, LICENSE, and executable, but no complete integrated yq clone was demonstrated.
parallel.verification: Workflow children were asked to record behavior and cases; official evaluation completed afterward but failed at compile before running tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out at about 2399 seconds and the official evaluator reported compile_failed with zero of 2046 tests run.

serial.requirements: Build the same original yq-compatible executable from observed behavior and bundled documentation under the same no-source/no-wrapper/no-binary-analysis rules.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single parent owned probing, implementation, integration, and packaging because workflows and task/delegation tools were disabled.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote a broader direct Go implementation, including node, scalar, YAML decode/encode, lexer, parser, eval, and core operator files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Submission packaging succeeded with a broader internal/yq tree plus compile.sh, go.mod, README, LICENSE, and executable.
serial.verification: Serial performed local direct work but official evaluation still failed at compile and ran no tests, so whole-task acceptance was absent.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out at about 2399 seconds and delivered a compile-failed submission despite broader source coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the reverse-engineering task and yq/YAML behavior surface, including the no-source and no-wrapper constraints, then delegated behavior discovery by feature area.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same original reimplementation obligation and began constructing a Go yq clone directly from observed behavior and bundled documentation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the material difference was how the parallel run converted the large behavior surface into delegated probes while serial stayed integrated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed exploration into a workflow with one area prompt per feature group and child agents started repeatedly under the workflow journal.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows and task tools disabled, so the single parent owned probing, implementation, and packaging without child handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel invested ownership in a broad research fan-out; serial used a single integrated owner for the whole implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief carried shared rules and per-area instructions, asking children for notes and tests rather than interoperating source components.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context local in one actor and did not need cross-agent contracts or returned child handoffs for implementation interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No specific missing child requirement or cross-agent interface defect explains the failure; the context boundary mostly shows broad delegation rather than incompatible handoff content.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After the workflow, the parent wrote a module skeleton and a small partial set of source files such as node.go, yamlparse.go, and resolve.go near the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the module skeleton and a broader implementation set including lexer, parser, eval, ops_core, YAML decode/encode, and scalar files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial achieved broader direct source coverage, while parallel's implementation path was narrower and later after the fan-out, but neither reached compilable correctness.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow produced many child actor records and child start journal entries; no clean complete implementation-result lifecycle reached integrated acceptance before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because delegation was disabled and all implementation work stayed in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried child lifecycle overhead and repeated starts; serial avoided join/retrieval overhead but still timed out on direct coding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The packaged artifact contained a small source tree with main.go, compile.sh, go.mod, README, tests, and a few internal/yq files; children also wrote notes/tests in the shared workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact contained a broader internal/yq source set plus compile.sh, go.mod, README, LICENSE, and executable, all produced by the single parent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace did not show a concrete collision, but the delivered implementation was materially smaller than serial's integrated source tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel requested children to generate tests and a harness, but the official evaluator later failed at compile and ran none of 2046 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also reached official compile failure with all 2046 tests not run despite writing more implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run produced evaluator-aligned acceptance evidence; the visible difference is that parallel verification effort was dispersed through delegated cases while serial verification stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 43 subagents, 870 workflow-child tool calls, and 1,887,376 workflow-child tokens, then the agent command returned 143 after about 2399 seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and 70 direct tool calls, but also timed out at about 2399 seconds with process return code 143.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the wall-clock budget, but parallel spent a large share on child fan-out before parent implementation, while serial spent its budget directly in one trajectory.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records make this pair both_fail, not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false, compile_failed, and 0 of 2046 tests run. The concrete task-solving difference is process and coverage rather than official pass/fail: parallel spent a large portion of its finite budget on workflow fan-out and repeated child starts before writing a smaller partial implementation, while serial kept one integrated owner and wrote more source files directly. That difference is adverse to the parallel process but did not create an outcome differential because the serial implementation also failed to compile.
parallel_contributors: Workflow fan-out across many behavior areas plus repeated child starts consumed budget before integrated implementation and verification matured.
Parent implementation writes were late and limited to a few core files before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided child lifecycle overhead and produced a broader internal/yq source tree directly.
Serial still exhausted the wall-clock budget and failed compile, so its integrated path was insufficient for a pass.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both submissions were incomplete yq reimplementations that failed at compile before any official tests could run.
Serial's broader file set did not establish correctness or compilability; this remains ordinary implementation failure outside the parallel taxonomy.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed with all 2046 tests marked not_run, so testcase behavior differences are not observable from evaluator results.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process contributor only

Rejected: there was no single mandatory preflight oracle or harness gate blocking all productive work; the adverse event was broad parallel fan-out.
Rejected: investigation did precede late implementation, but the concrete adverse boundary was the excessive breadth and repeated child starts exhausting budget.
Rejected: this was not a general underallocation of an otherwise clear critical path; collective fan-out budget exhaustion is the more specific load-imbalance event.

The parent launched a broad workflow for yq behavior exploration, the script fans out AREAS.map agent calls across feature areas, the journal records child starts through line 43, and status/cell metadata show 43 child logs plus the fixed 2399-second timeout before a complete implementation or verification loop.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad workflow fan-out and child restarts consumed the finite run budget, leaving only partial parent source writes near the deadline and a compile-failed packaged submission.
candidates.near_match_reason: Critical-path capacity was affected, but the specific direct boundary is collective fan-out breadth and retries exhausting the budget rather than a simple allocation of too few workers to one path.

Serial did not delegate and spent its budget on direct implementation writes, so this is a parallel-side adverse coordination pattern even though both official outcomes failed.
